answer: One defence is an on-device biometric uniqueness proof: to register, an agent's owner passes a liveness scan, and only a salted hash of the template ever leaves the phone, so no raw biometric is exposed. Like one tree per plot in an orchard, each person can root exactly one identity; a second registration with the same template is rejected network-wide. A Sybil farmer would therefore need a new real human for every fake, the way a bridge needs a fresh karst footing on each bank — the price of one more fake becomes the price of recruiting one more person, not of running one more script.
